Read, write, delete and list a sandbox's files.

## Read a file

`GET /v1/sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files` (SDK method `readFile`)

A file of up to 1 MiB, as UTF-8 text unless `encoding` asks for base64. A larger file is read in parts of up to 1 MiB with `offset` and `length`; `size` in the answer is the whole file's. Use base64 for a part of a binary file, or of a text file cut mid-character. A key needs `files`.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandboxId` | string | yes | The sandbox's ID. |

**Query parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes |  |
| `encoding` | [FileEncoding](/api/reference/types/#fileencoding) | no |  |
| `offset` | integer | no | Read from this byte (default 0). With `offset` or `length`, a file of any size is read a part at a time. (minimum 0) |
| `length` | integer | no | Read at most this many bytes: default, and at most, 1 MiB (1048576). (minimum 1, maximum 1048576) |

**Answers**

- `200`: [FileContent](/api/reference/types/#filecontent) (`application/json`). The file.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found, `409` conflict. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Write a file

`PUT /v1/sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files` (SDK method `writeFile`)

Writes a file, making its directories, replacing what was there. A key needs `files`.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandboxId` | string | yes | The sandbox's ID. |

**Body**: [WriteFileBody](/api/reference/types/#writefilebody)

**Answers**

- `200`: [FileEntry](/api/reference/types/#fileentry) (`application/json`). The file written.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found, `409` conflict. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Delete a file

`DELETE /v1/sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files` (SDK method `deleteFile`)

Deletes a file, or a directory and everything in it. A key needs `files`.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandboxId` | string | yes | The sandbox's ID. |

**Query parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes | An absolute path, or one relative to a microVM's `/home/user` or an isolate's `/workspace`. |

**Answers**

- `204`: no body. Deleted.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found, `409` conflict. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Write a part of a file

`PUT /v1/sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files/parts` (SDK method `writeFilePart`)

A file goes up in parts, in any order and at once if you like, each the raw bytes from its `offset`, under an `upload` ID of yours; then one completion with its size and SHA-256. Nothing is at `path` until the completion has checked both, and then the file replaces what was there in one step. microVMs only. A part is the request's raw body, at most 64 MiB (67108864 bytes); the file is at most 64 GiB, and no more than the sandbox's disk has free (`exhausted`). Sending a part again writes it again. The parts are kept beside the file, on the sandbox's disk, until the upload is completed or aborted; an upload with no part for an hour, and every upload of a sandbox that stops without its memory, is discarded. A key needs `files`.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandboxId` | string | yes | The sandbox's ID. |

**Query parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes | The file's path: absolute, or relative to a microVM's `/home/user`. Not in or over a mount. (at most 4096 characters) |
| `upload` | string | yes | Your name for this upload, 8 to 64 letters, digits, `-` or `_`, such as a UUID: the same on each of its parts and its completion. A new one for each upload. |
| `offset` | integer | yes | The byte of the file this part starts at. (minimum 0, maximum 68719476736) |

**Answers**

- `200`: [FilePart](/api/reference/types/#filepart) (`application/json`). The part written.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found, `409` conflict, `429` exhausted, `501` not_supported, `503` unavailable. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Abort a file written in parts

`DELETE /v1/sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files/parts` (SDK method `abortFileParts`)

Discards an upload's parts. What is at `path` is untouched. An upload that isn't known is fine too. A key needs `files`.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandboxId` | string | yes | The sandbox's ID. |

**Query parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes | The file's path: absolute, or relative to a microVM's `/home/user`. Not in or over a mount. (at most 4096 characters) |
| `upload` | string | yes | Your name for this upload, 8 to 64 letters, digits, `-` or `_`, such as a UUID: the same on each of its parts and its completion. A new one for each upload. |

**Answers**

- `204`: no body. Discarded.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found, `409` conflict, `501` not_supported, `503` unavailable. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Complete a file written in parts

`POST /v1/sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files/parts/complete` (SDK method `completeFileParts`)

Checks that the parts written come to `size` bytes with the SHA-256 `sha256`, then moves the file into place with `mode` (default `0644`), owned by the sandbox's user, replacing what was at `path`. A check that fails is `invalid`, and the upload is discarded with nothing at `path`: send it again under a new `upload` ID. Completing again answers as the first time while `path` still has that size and SHA-256, so a lost answer can be asked for again; an upload that isn't known is `conflict`. A key needs `files`.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandboxId` | string | yes | The sandbox's ID. |

**Body**: [CompleteFilePartsBody](/api/reference/types/#completefilepartsbody)

**Answers**

- `200`: [FileEntry](/api/reference/types/#fileentry) (`application/json`). The file written.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found, `409` conflict, `501` not_supported, `503` unavailable. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Get an upload URL for a file

`POST /v1/sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files/upload-url` (SDK method `createUploadUrl`)

A short-lived URL on the API, streamed straight to the sandbox's host: `PUT` the file to it as the raw request body, of any size, with no `Authorization` header; the answer is `{ path, size }`. Missing directories are made, and a file already there is replaced only once the upload is complete. The URL is bound to this sandbox and path, and expires after `ttlSeconds`. A path in a read-only mount is refused (`conflict`). The sandbox must be running when the URL is used. Treat it as a secret. A key needs `files`. Experimental: `not_supported` unless the deployment has turned mounts on (`KANTEL_MOUNTS=experimental`).

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandboxId` | string | yes | The sandbox's ID. |

**Body**: [FileUrlBody](/api/reference/types/#fileurlbody)

**Answers**

- `200`: [FileUrl](/api/reference/types/#fileurl) (`application/json`). The URL.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found, `409` conflict, `501` not_supported. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Get a download URL for a file

`POST /v1/sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files/download-url` (SDK method `createDownloadUrl`)

A short-lived URL on the API, streamed straight from the sandbox's host: `GET` it, with no `Authorization` header, for the file's bytes as they are when it is fetched, whatever its size (`HEAD` for its size alone). The URL is bound to this sandbox and path, and expires after `ttlSeconds`. The sandbox must be running when the URL is used. Treat it as a secret. A key needs `files`. Experimental: `not_supported` unless the deployment has turned mounts on (`KANTEL_MOUNTS=experimental`).

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandboxId` | string | yes | The sandbox's ID. |

**Body**: [FileUrlBody](/api/reference/types/#fileurlbody)

**Answers**

- `200`: [FileUrl](/api/reference/types/#fileurl) (`application/json`). The URL.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found, `409` conflict, `501` not_supported. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Extract an archive into a directory

`PUT /v1/sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files/archive` (SDK method `extractArchive`)

Writes every file, directory and symbolic link of a tar (or a gzipped tar) into `path`, in one call. An entry whose name is absolute or climbs out of `path` (`..`), a link that points out of it, an entry under such a link, and hard links, devices and FIFOs are refused (`invalid`) before anything is written. A `path` in a read-only mount, or with one under it, is refused (`conflict`). Files are owned by the sandbox's user, with their modes from the tar. A key needs `files`. Experimental: `not_supported` unless the deployment has turned mounts on (`KANTEL_MOUNTS=experimental`).

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sandboxId` | string | yes | The sandbox's ID. |

**Query parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes | The directory to extract into, made if missing: absolute, or relative to a microVM's `/home/user`. Not in or over a mount. (at most 4096 characters) |

**Answers**

- `200`: [ExtractedArchive](/api/reference/types/#extractedarchive) (`application/json`). What was extracted.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found, `409` conflict, `501` not_supported, `503` unavailable. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).
